lens: Gawande — operational correctness of the wired lane progress rule

findings.summary: A stop can kill a command younger than W after a checkpoint request was delivered.
evidence: ProgressRule.on_tick checks commands_in_flight only when the request is None or deferred; with a delivered request it falls through to stop even when a command is in flight.
After a request is delivered at W, the resumed lane can start a command just before 2W. Command start is not progress, so the next check stops the lane and kills that command after only a short run.
The deferred-command unit test starts its command before the first check; it does not cover a command started after request delivery.
findings.action: Apply the in-flight age rule to stop actions too. Track command start times and defer a kill until the active command has run at least W; add a real pipe/process test for a command started late in the request window.

findings.summary: An unobservable worktree makes every command completion count as progress.
evidence: ProgressRule._on_complete increments _new_outcomes and returns whenever the fingerprint is None, without checking whether the command/tree pair is new.
Repeated commands on an unreadable worktree therefore reset each progress window indefinitely, although the spec says an unobservable worktree contributes neither progress nor its absence.
The unobservable-worktree test covers a file-change event and silence, but not repeated command completions.
findings.action: Count a command completion as progress only when its fingerprint is observable and its pair is new. Add a test with repeated identical completions while the fingerprint remains None.

findings.summary: Persistent watcher errors can leave a lane running forever.
evidence: LaneProgressWatch._run catches any exception from tick and continues polling without recording a fault or stopping the executor.

An exception before ProgressRule.on_tick, such as a persistent steer-queue read or log-read failure, can prevent every check from reaching the rule. With the wall-clock default removed, no other timer reclaims the lane.
findings.action: Make an unrecoverable or repeated watch failure produce a recorded terminal stop and kill, or provide an independent bounded reclamation path. Test a persistent polling failure.

findings.summary: Preemption and stop side effects are not serialized, so a losing preemption can still queue a steer and count as delivered work.
evidence: observe_event obtains an action from ProgressRule and calls _apply after the rule lock is released; the watch thread can meanwhile reach _stop_now, which uses a separate lock.

_apply does not recheck stop_reason or coordinate with _stop_now. It can enqueue a steer, set _preempted, increment preemptions, and kill after the stop has already won; _execute_codex then sees stop_reason and exits before delivering the queued steer.
take_preempted returns one boolean per invocation, while LaneProgressWatch.preemptions increments per _apply call, so overlapping actions can also disagree in their receipts.
findings.action: Serialize action delivery and stop under one first-wins state transition. Suppress and account for actions that lose to stop; add a deterministic race test covering queue state, preemption count, and final result.

findings.summary: A lane ending after a checkpoint request is not recorded as answering it.
evidence: ProgressRule._mark_answered is called only when a later progress check observes progress; there is no finish/finalization method for a normal final report or BLOCKED turn ending.
LaneProgressWatch.stop halts polling but does not resolve the delivered request, so the receipt can leave answered absent even when the executor ended as the spec defines an answer.
findings.action: Add a lane-finish transition that records a delivered request as answered when the lane ends with its final report or BLOCKED response, and test that receipt outcome.

counterweight_triage.concern: LP-1 exact command-text loop keys can be evaded by varying command text.
counterweight_triage.disposition: Accepted as the spec's explicit non-claim; not treated as a new implementation blocker.

counterweight_triage.concern: A missing watch when the progress window is zero.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The spec explicitly allows W=0 to disable the rule; this is not an accidental missing-watch path.

counterweight_triage.concern: Whether tests reach a pipe and process.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The fake Codex integration tests run a subprocess through StampingPipe and exercise process-group kill/resume. They do not cover the late-start command stop, watcher-failure path, or action races, and do not establish live Codex or Muse session behavior.

counterweight_triage.concern: Attempt and WIP classification downstream of the selected execution paths.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The execution loop distinguishes ordinary preemption from failed session resume and subtracts preemptions from relaunch friction, but the attempt/checkpoint owners are outside the selected input; no claim is made that downstream WIP classification is proven.

next_move: Fix the late-start kill, unknown-fingerprint command accounting, watcher failure handling, and action/stop serialization; add focused process-level and deterministic race tests, then finalize request-answer receipts and re-review the wired behavior.
non_claims: LP-1 remains a recorded non-claim and was not re-litigated as a defect.
Live Codex and Muse resume semantics were not established by these fake-executor tests.
Downstream attempt and WIP classification was not established because its owners are outside the selected paths.
